inputs_read: canonical WEB Lamentations text and coordinates

non_authority_declaration: No theology, canon, authorship, date, historical reconstruction, ethics, divine agency, fulfillment, community identity, preferred translation, or preferred witness decision.
Acrostic form, Hebrew evidence, meter, voice labels, and internal biblical relations are evidence only.
Speaker labels are provisional; ambiguity is preserved.

method.unit_preference: Prefer the larger coherent movement and retain the complete poem as macro parent.
anti_atomization_guards: Do not split every alphabetic stanza.
Do not atomize loss or reversal catalogues.
Do not isolate 3:22-24 or 3:31-33 as proof texts.
Do not use chapter coordinates alone.
If voice/addressee is disputed, retain the larger alternative and LOW confidence.

macro_parent_alternatives.form: alphabetic city lament with narrator, personified-city speech, and closing petition
macro_parent_alternatives.retention_rule: Retain all children under the complete poem; disputed seams collapse to the full poem.
principal_ambiguities: Embedded cries at 1:9 and 1:11 may anticipate sustained speech at 1:12.
1:17 is a narrator bridge that may group backward or forward.

macro_parent_alternatives.form: alphabetic lament from destruction catalogue through grief and exhortation to petition
macro_parent_alternatives.retention_rule: Disputed seams may collapse to 2:18-22 or the full poem.
principal_ambiguities: Subject and voice at 2:18 are difficult.
Speaker at 2:20-22 may be Zion, communal, or poetic continuation.

macro_parent_alternatives.form: triple-acrostic individual lament opening into wisdom, communal confession, recollection, and appeal
macro_parent_alternatives.retention_rule: Group rather than atomize sixty-six lines; disputed seams collapse to 3:19-39, 3:40-51, 3:52-66, or the full poem.
principal_ambiguities: Afflicted speaker identity and representativeness remain unresolved.
Singular/plural transitions do not prove new speakers.
Pit recollection is not a historical-identity warrant.

macro_parent_alternatives.form: alphabetic reversal lament through siege, indictment, pursuit, and two-city coda
macro_parent_alternatives.retention_rule: Disputed seams may collapse to 4:1-16, 4:17-22, or the full poem.
principal_ambiguities: 4:11-12 may close the siege catalogue or open the indictment.
Plural at 4:17 identifies no historical group.

macro_parent_alternatives.form: twenty-two-line communal prayer from invocation/catalogue to closing address
macro_parent_alternatives.retention_rule: Because the catalogue is cumulative, disputed seams collapse to the full poem.
principal_ambiguities: Direct address starts at 5:1, so 5:19 renews rather than begins prayer.
5:22 remains part of the appeal under every interpretation.

chunks.title: The solitary city: loss, exile, and remembered former splendor
chunks.literary_form: third-person alphabetic city-lament movement
chunks.deciding_marker: Sustained third-person city/Judah description; 1:7 completes memory and mockery before shame and embedded appeal intensify.
chunks.rejected_alternative: Reject 1:1-11 as the only opening unit and reject one-verse acrostic atomization.
chunks.risk: 1:7-8 is only a meso seam inside the intact poem; it proves no speaker, source, or historical layer.

chunks.title: Jerusalem's shame, sanctuary violation, hunger, and embedded cries to be seen
chunks.literary_form: third-person shame-and-loss catalogue with embedded first-person appeals
chunks.deciding_marker: Shame, defilement, invasion, and hunger frame brief repeated imperatives; sustained personified-city speech begins clearly at 1:12.
chunks.rejected_alternative: Reject starting a separate sustained speech at 1:9 or 1:11 and reject isolating either brief quotation.
chunks.risk: Speech onset is ambiguous; 1:9b or 1:11b could already voice Zion, so retain the whole-poem parent.

chunks.title: Zion addresses passersby and recounts the blows against her
chunks.literary_form: sustained first-person personified-city lament and public address
chunks.deciding_marker: The address to passersby initiates sustained first-person speech; 1:16 closes its image-chain with tears before the third-person bridge at 1:17.
chunks.rejected_alternative: Reject isolating 1:12 or splitting fire, net, yoke, assembly, winepress, and tears.
chunks.risk: Personified Zion is provisional description, not identity; the speech could begin at 1:9 or 1:11.

chunks.title: Narrator bridge and Zion's confession, distress, and closing appeal
chunks.literary_form: third-person bridge into first-person confession and petition
chunks.deciding_marker: 1:17 briefly resumes third-person observation; 1:18-22 sustains address to peoples and Yahweh, closing with petition.
chunks.rejected_alternative: Reject a one-verse 1:17 chunk and reject atomizing confession, failed lovers, distress, enemies, and closing appeal.
chunks.risk: 1:17 could close the prior movement or introduce the next; larger 1:12-22 remains viable.

chunks.title: The destruction of Zion, her institutions, walls, leaders, and worship
chunks.literary_form: third-person divine-destruction catalogue within alphabetic lament
chunks.deciding_marker: Repeated third-person clauses move through city, sanctuary, wall, gates, leaders, and mourners; explicit observer grief begins at 2:11.
chunks.rejected_alternative: Reject splitting at 2:5, 2:6, or 2:8 by image or institutional subtype; the catalogue is cumulative.
chunks.risk: Internal escalations do not outweigh continuity; divine-agency wording authorizes no theological or ethical ruling.

chunks.title: The observer's tears, dying children, and unanswerable address to Zion
chunks.literary_form: first-person witness lament turning to apostrophe and rhetorical questions
chunks.deciding_marker: My eyes/my heart shifts to observer grief; 2:13 directly addresses daughter Jerusalem and closes in an unanswerable question.
chunks.rejected_alternative: Reject isolating the child-hunger scene or detaching 2:13 from the observer's compassionate address.
chunks.risk: The observer is unidentified, and 2:13 could open the next address movement.

chunks.title: Failed visions, public scorn, enemy triumph, and destruction summarized
chunks.literary_form: second-person accusation and taunt catalogue with summary declaration
chunks.deciding_marker: Failed visions, passersby, and enemies escalate to 2:17's summary before the exhortation to cry at 2:18.
chunks.rejected_alternative: Reject separate chunks for prophets, passersby, enemies, and the summary declaration.
chunks.risk: 2:17 may close the initial destruction catalogue; its wording cannot authorize fulfillment or chronology.

chunks.title: Summons to ceaseless tears and night prayer for the children
chunks.literary_form: exhortation to communal lament and prayer
chunks.deciding_marker: Imperatives to weep, arise, cry, pour out the heart, and lift hands form one summons; direct first-person petition follows at 2:20.
chunks.rejected_alternative: Reject isolating disputed 2:18 or separating night prayer from its child-focused purpose.
chunks.risk: The subject and voice of 2:18 are difficult; 2:18-22 is the safer larger alternative if the seam fails.

chunks.title: Final appeal over siege horrors, slaughter, and no survivor
chunks.literary_form: direct divine-address petition and closing lament
chunks.deciding_marker: Look, Yahweh opens sustained second-person address and questions, closing with the assembly-terror reversal and loss of those reared.
chunks.rejected_alternative: Reject isolating 2:20's horrors or dividing age-group and terror catalogues.
chunks.risk: The speaker may be Zion, communal voice, or another poetic voice; no identity or divine-agency judgment is made.

chunks.title: The afflicted speaker enclosed in darkness, hostility, ridicule, and lost expectation
chunks.literary_form: first-person individual lament in triple-acrostic sequence
chunks.deciding_marker: I am the man opens sustained bodily, spatial, animal, military, and social affliction, ending with lost strength and expectation.
chunks.rejected_alternative: Reject every three-verse alphabetic block or metaphor as a separate chunk.
chunks.risk: Speaker identity and representativeness are unresolved; 3:17-18 could join the remembrance movement.

chunks.title: Remembered bitterness recalled into hope and confession of Yahweh as portion
chunks.literary_form: remembrance-to-hope hinge within individual lament
chunks.deciding_marker: Repeated remembering turns at 3:21 to deliberate recall and hope, reaching the portion-and-hope confession at 3:24.
chunks.rejected_alternative: Reject extracting 3:22-24 as an independent hopeful proof text; it depends on 3:19-21.
chunks.risk: Singular/plural language and the translation of 3:22 are disputed; no preferred reading or speaker shift is decided.

chunks.title: Wisdom reflection on waiting, bearing, compassion, justice, and complaint
chunks.literary_form: wisdom instruction and rhetorical reflection
chunks.deciding_marker: General statements about what is good move through generic imperatives, reasons about grief and justice, and closing rhetorical questions.
chunks.rejected_alternative: Reject isolating 3:31-33 or splitting the justice triad 3:34-36 from surrounding wisdom questions.
chunks.risk: The syntax and scope of 3:34-39 admit alternatives; this grouping decides no theology, theodicy, or translation.

chunks.title: Communal self-examination, return, confession, and affliction
chunks.literary_form: communal exhortation turning to plural confession and lament
chunks.deciding_marker: Let us search/turn/lift begins a communal movement; plural confession and accusation close in terror, pit, devastation, and destruction.
chunks.rejected_alternative: Reject dividing exhortation 3:40-41 from confession 3:42-47.
chunks.risk: Plural voice identifies no historical community and may continue through singular tears at 3:48-51.

chunks.title: Unceasing tears for the destruction of the speaker's people
chunks.literary_form: first-person tear-lament and watch for divine regard
chunks.deciding_marker: Repeated my-eye language binds unceasing tears, waiting until Yahweh sees, and grief for the city; pursuit begins at 3:52.
chunks.rejected_alternative: Reject one-verse tear fragments or treating 3:50 as an isolated hope saying.
chunks.risk: Singular voice may be the afflicted speaker, a representative, or modulation; 3:40-51 is safer if disputed.

chunks.title: Pursuit, the pit, invocation, heard prayer, nearness, and rescue
chunks.literary_form: recollection of mortal peril turning to testimony of answered appeal
chunks.deciding_marker: Past pursuit-and-pit recollection turns to invocation at 3:55 and reaches rescue at 3:58 before renewed judicial appeal.
chunks.rejected_alternative: Reject splitting the pit scene at 3:54 or separating invocation from hearing, nearness, reassurance, and rescue.
chunks.risk: The scene may be literal, metaphorical, or poetic and cannot identify the speaker or harmonize another narrative.

chunks.title: Closing appeal for judgment against reproach, plots, and pursuers
chunks.literary_form: direct divine-address judicial appeal and imprecatory close
chunks.deciding_marker: Judge my cause renews direct appeal; repeated you have seen/heard leads to the closing request or expectation of requital.
chunks.rejected_alternative: Reject separate chunks for sight, hearing, mockery, recompense, curse, and pursuit.
chunks.risk: Verb forms in 3:64-66 admit alternatives; the unit selects no reading or ethical/theological judgment.

chunks.title: Gold, children, nobles, and mothers reversed under siege famine
chunks.literary_form: alphabetic reversal catalogue and siege lament
chunks.deciding_marker: How and reversal comparisons accumulate from sanctuary stones through children, luxury, nobles, starvation, and maternal horror at 4:10.
chunks.rejected_alternative: Reject social-group atomization and seams at 4:6 or 4:7.
chunks.risk: Comparative evaluation and severe images remain inside the cumulative lament; no historical or ethical conclusion follows.

chunks.title: Wrath, breached Jerusalem, blood-guilt, pollution, and dispersed leaders
chunks.literary_form: causal religious-social indictment and dispersal sequence
chunks.deciding_marker: 4:11-12 bridge from siege to breach; because at 4:13 introduces prophets/priests, blood pollution, exclusion, wandering, and scattering.
chunks.rejected_alternative: Reject isolating 4:11-12 or separating prophets, priests, pollution cries, and scattering.
chunks.risk: 4:11-12 may close the siege unit and 4:15's voice is uncertain; no group-authority or historical ruling is made.

chunks.title: Our vain watch for help, hunted steps, swift pursuers, and captured anointed one
chunks.literary_form: first-person plural communal pursuit lament
chunks.deciding_marker: Our begins failed help, hunted movement, approaching end, pursuit, ambush, and capture of the figure under whose shadow the group hoped to live.
chunks.rejected_alternative: Reject splitting foreign help, street pursuit, wilderness ambush, and the captured anointed figure.
chunks.risk: The community, nation, and anointed figure are not identified or dated; cross-references cannot force reconstruction.

chunks.title: Edom and Zion addressed in a two-city closing coda
chunks.literary_form: paired direct-address oracle-like lament coda
chunks.deciding_marker: Vocatives to daughter Edom and daughter Zion, cup imagery, and paired statements of visitation/non-continuation form a contrastive close.
chunks.rejected_alternative: Reject separating the Edom address from the Zion address.
chunks.risk: Force, time reference, and referents remain unresolved; the coda decides no fulfillment, chronology, theology, or reading.

chunks.title: Communal invocation and cumulative catalogue of dispossession, violence, toil, and lost joy
chunks.literary_form: communal prayer opening with imperative and unfolding as affliction catalogue
chunks.deciding_marker: Remember/look frame a sustained plural catalogue of inheritance/family loss, forced labor, hunger, violence, civic collapse, mourning, confession, and Zion's desolation.
chunks.rejected_alternative: Reject splitting by social group, resource, age, or image; 5:17-18 summarize the catalogue before renewed address.
chunks.risk: Internal escalations at 5:7-8, 5:11, and 5:15-16 support smaller alternatives, but cumulative function favors the larger movement.

chunks.title: Yahweh's enduring throne and the closing questions and petition for return
chunks.literary_form: renewed direct divine address, rhetorical protest, and closing petition
chunks.deciding_marker: You, Yahweh renews sustained address, followed by a why-question, the imperative to turn/renew, and a severe final qualification.
chunks.rejected_alternative: Reject isolating 5:19, 5:21, or 5:22 as detached praise, restoration, or rejection sayings.
chunks.risk: The relation and translation of 5:22 are disputed; no preferred translation, theology, or liturgical resolution is selected.
